 now 16.25 EST Antonio Nusa is some footballer, by the way. If you’re looking for your next major import to the Premier League from the Leipzig talent factory – a la Benjamin Sesko, Josko Gvardiol, Dominik Szoboszlai, Christopher Nkunku et al – the Norwegian winger is a very solid bet.
 Share 2m ago 16.23 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 2-2 Manchester City (Nusa, 61)
 What a game this is! City’s lead does not last long this time as Leipzig work it to Antonio Nusa on the left side of the box, and he does not disappoint with a low left-footed finish.
 Enzo Maresca’s side look suddenly porous at the back and Leipzig have what they deserve … again.
 View image in fullscreen Antonio Nusa equalises for Leipzig! Photograph: Maja Hitij/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.25 EST 4m ago 16.20 EST 6-0 to Como. I can’t keep up. Douvikas completes his hat-trick, and takes his UCL season’s tally to six in the process. This could be a cricket score. It’s already a tennis score.
 Share 5m ago 16.19 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 1-2 Manchester City (Fernández, 58)
 City have restored their lead in no time! Ndiaye teases home a superb cross that was begging to be met … and Enzo Fernández is the man! He powers home a clinical headed finish.
 View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernandez restores the Man City lead. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.23 EST 6m ago 16.18 EST Honestly, Como are making a mockery of this competition – or maybe just of Lens. It’s now 5-0 to Fabregas’s fantastic team, Marc-Oliver Kempf getting in on the act. A classic case of getting in on the act, actually.
 Share 8m ago 16.17 EST GOAL! PSV 1-1 Club Brugge (Sano, 54)
 This has been another really enjoyable game, from the bits I’ve seen, and PSV have found a fortunate equaliser via Japanese international midfielder Kodai Sano. He squeezed home after an almighty deflection.
 Share 10m ago 16.14 EST GOAL! Borussia Dortmund 1-0 Real Betis (Silva, 49)
 After a watchable but goalless first half, the breakthrough at Signal Iduna Park arrives for the home side, with Fabio Silva scoring a poacher’s goal after Jobe Bellingham’s shot was blocked in the box.
 Real Betis’s perfect Champions League record this season is now at serious risk. As it stands, only PSG and Real Madrid will have four wins under their belts.
 View image in fullscreen Wolves legend Fabio Silva puts Dortmund in front against Betis. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP Share Updated at  16.21 EST 12m ago 16.13 EST This is probably a case of speaking way too soon , but it’s been refreshing not to see too many fastidious VAR checks for handball or other types of dubious penalty shout. The early rounds of this Champions League group stage were riddled with such occurrences.
 Share 13m ago 16.11 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 1-1 Manchester City (Baku, 49)
 That was coming! Another rapid Leipzig breaks sees the white shirts flood forward and this time Donnarumma is at fault. Somehow he’s let a cross from Ridle Baku in at the near post … talk about from hero to zero!
 He should have done a lot better with that, it was simple fare for elite goalkeepers, usually gobbled up.
 Share 15m ago 16.10 EST It’s an absolute procession for Como in Lens as Da Cunha drills home from Nico Paz’s pass to make it 4-0. This Italian team have come to play in this season’s Champions League . Lens are done.
 Share 16m ago 16.08 EST What a save from Donnarumma to deny Christoph Baumgartner. That shot was bound for the top right corner before the Italian sprung high and got an important fingertip to it.
 Leipzig are growing a little frustrated that their attacking efforts have had no reward thus far.
 Share 18m ago 16.06 EST Manchester City are lucky to be ahead in Leipzig, and you sense they will have to step up in the second half to avoid another winless 90 minutes. They cannot seem to get Erling Haaland in the game, chances for any of their forwards in fact have been scant.
 Arsenal’s opponents are more lightweight than Leipzig, but still the Gunners’ sharpness going forward has been notable, despite Mikel Arteta resting the likes of Kai Havertz, Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis so far.
 The second halves are mostly under way around Europe. Let’s get into the updates again. 
 Share 24m ago 16.01 EST Here are the reports from the earlier games.
 Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapses Read more Valverde’s late winner breaks AEK Athens hearts as Real Madrid twice come from behind Read more Share 33m ago 15.51 EST Half-time scores
 Borussia Dortmund 0-0 Real Betis
 Lens 0-3 Como
 PSV 0-1 Club Brugge
 Porto 1-1 Napoli
 RB Leipzig 0-1 Manchester City
 Slavia Prague 0-2 Arsenal
 Viking 1-1 Sabah
 And right there, after a hectic 45 minutes typing, I shall take the shortest of breaks! Plenty more fun to be had in the second halves.
 Share Updated at  15.51 EST 36m ago 15.48 EST The half-time whistles are starting to sound. We’ll round up all the scores soon.
 Share 38m ago 15.46 EST GOAL! Porto 1-1 Napoli (McTominay, 43)
 Napoli had wasted a couple of chances to get level in Porto but Scott McTominay – who else? – has found an equaliser a few minutes before half-time. A great reactive rebound effort from the former Manchester United man.
 View image in fullscreen Scott McTominay levels for Napoli on the stroke of half-time. Photograph: Patrícia de Melo Moreira/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.53 EST 40m ago 15.45 EST Paz paid tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel with a t-shirt showing the player’s image, after scoring his goal. Paz grew up on Tenerife and was part of the club’s academy for two years as a boy.
 Share 42m ago 15.43 EST 3-0 to Como in Lens. Nico Paz. Cesc Fabregas is clearly the greatest football coach to have ever graced our good game.
 Share 42m ago 15.43 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 0-1 Manchester City (Lukeba OG, 37)
 City haven’t been at their scintillating best against Leipzig so far, but they’ve been handed the lead by an awful own goal by Castello Lukeba. There were a million things he could have done with Nico O’Reilly’s cutback … other than to bundle it into his own net.
 View image in fullscreen Castello Lukeba scores a fantastic own goal for Man City. Photograph: Annegret Hilse/Reuters Share Updated at  15.46 EST 44m ago 15.41 EST GOAL! Slavia Prague 0-2 Arsenal (Gyökeres, 38)
 Just when I thought I may be wrong about Arsenal in my earlier post , with the Slavia defence seemingly holding up well, Viktor Gyökeres slides one into the far corner after nice interplay with Mikel Merino. Two-nil and it will probably be more before long.
 View image in fullscreen A superb finish from Viktor Gyökeres to make it 2-0 to Arsenal. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share Updated at  15.44 EST 47m ago 15.37 EST Douvikas is now out on his own as the top-scorer in this season’s Champions League so far, with five goals.
 Tresoldi of Club Brugge is there on four alongside a tranche of star names, including Ballon D’Or’s Harry Kane, Erling Haaland, Dortmund hitman Guirassy and Roma’s Donyell Malen.
 We’ll keep tabs on that.
 Share 50m ago 15.35 EST Como have doubled their lead at Lens! Douvikas nets his second of the evening for Cesc Fabregas’s side, who are seriously enjoying life in the Champions League , aren’t they? (0-2)
 Share 53m ago 15.32 EST This isn’t Champions League-related, but a quick check of how West Ham are faring in their first game after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo and appointing Scott Parker … and they are 3-0 down at Cardiff City.
 Jack Moylan has bagged a hat-trick for the Bluebirds. Perhaps there will be no quick fix for the Hammers.
 View image in fullscreen Oh, West Ham. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at  15.35 EST 55m ago 15.30 EST Viking have levelled at home to Sabah, with Erik Botheim scoring an improvised volley. It’s 1-1 in Norway.
 Share 1h ago 15.29 EST GOAL! PSV 0-1 Club Brugge (Tresoldi, 25)
 Club Brugge have broken the deadlock in Eindhoven, and it’s their star striker Nicolò Tresoldi with a timely header. The young forward has been scoring by the boatload this season so it’s no surprise to see his name on the scoresheet.
 View image in fullscreen Nicolo Tresoldi opens the scoring for Club Brugge. Photograph: John Thys/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.34 EST 1h ago 15.26 EST It’s still goalless between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis but that appears to be the most open and even contest of this batch of fixtures, based on the opening exchanges. Both teams have squandered big chances, and there’s been that disallowed Antony strike. (0-0)
 Share 1h ago 15.23 EST RB Leipzig have been able to put together some very fast counterattacks to trouble Manchester City in the opening 20 minutes in Germany. That City midfield looks a little light tonight, with Elliot Anderson being asked to cover a lot of ground.
 City have failed to win their past three games in 90 minutes, remember. (0-0)
 View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson is challenged by Christoph Baumgartner in Leipzig. Photograph: Maja Hitij/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.30 EST 1h ago 15.21 EST “VAR in Europe drives me crazy,” exclaims Steve McManaman on TNT Sports, before changing tack and saying “good lad, well done” after a check for a handball in the Lens v Como goal is waved away. It would have been a framkly ludicrous penalty decision.
 Share 1h ago 15.19 EST Arsenal are peppering the Slavia Prague goal in these early stages. After getting that goal, the Gunners should find plenty of joy, with the hosts forced to push out and play a bit. I should be utterly stunned if Arsenal don’t score at least three or four.
 Share 1h ago 15.19 EST Antony thinks he’s scored for Real Betis at Dortmund after being found by Troy Parrott… VAR has a long old check of it. No goal. The former Manchester United player’s goal drought goes on.
 Share 1h ago 15.15 EST I’m afraid I don’t have the bandwidth to stay across Viking v Sabah with detailed updates, but the visitors have opened the scoring via Gabonese forward Orphé Mbina. (0-1)
 Share 1h ago 15.14 EST GOAL! Porto 1-0 Napoli (Bednarek, 11)
 Porto are winless so far in this season’s Champions League but they are ahead inside 11 minutes at home to Napoli. A simple header from Jan Bednarek from a corner gets the home fans going at the Estádio do Dragão.
 View image in fullscreen Former Southampton man Jan Bednarek fires Porto in front against Napoli. Photograph: Octávio Passos/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.18 EST 1h ago 15.13 EST Madueke looks like a player reborn this season, doesn’t he? Surely he will feature in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad later this month? The winger has found a clinical touch in front of goal, which was so often a criticism levelled at him.
 Share 1h ago 15.12 EST GOAL! Slavia Prague 0-1 Arsenal (Madueke, 9)
 Arsenal follow suit after some less-than-impressive Slavia Prague defending. A long ball downfield is not defended, before Noni Madueke is slipped in by Viktor Gyökeres… and slips it past the goalkeeper.
 View image in fullscreen Noni Madueke scores for Arsenal! Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.16 EST 1h ago 15.10 EST GOAL! Lens 0-1 Como (Douvikas, 7)
 And there is the first goal! Como are making a mockery of their ‘Champions League debutants’ tag this season. Anastasios Douvikas has turned in after a well-worked short corner was eventually nodded down in the box.
 View image in fullscreen Anastasios Douvikas opens the scoring for high-flying Como. Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/Reuters Share Updated at  15.13 EST 1h ago 15.09 EST Serhou Guirassy has a sensational scoring record in the Champions League for Borussia Dortmund and he might have done better with an early chance, failing to latch on to Julian Ryerson’s cross from the right.
 We’re still goalless across the board after around 6 minutes.
 Share 1h ago 15.07 EST It’s a night for Premier League teams to be taking on teams managed by their former players. After Dirk Kuyt downed Liverpool earlier on, can Martin Demichelis do something similar to his old side Manchester City? The former Argentina centre-back is in charge of RB Leipzig these days.
 Share 1h ago 15.03 EST KICK OFF
 Whistles are sounded around Europe to signal the start of tonight’s late action! We’ll bring you all the goals as they go in …
 Share 1h ago 15.02 EST All the grounds have held a minute’s silence in memory of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who tragically died at the age of 30 after he suffered a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters Share Updated at  15.05 EST 2h ago 14.54 EST Mikel Arteta has been speaking to TNT Sports before kick-off in Prague. 
 “We need everybody, everybody has a big impact on the team,” he says on his decision to rotate his lineup. “We know the patterns we’re going to have tonight against this opponent.”
 On whether William Saliba could feature off the bench, he says: “Let’s see how the game pans out. He’s only had a couple of sessions with us, let’s be patient.”
 Share 2h ago 14.51 EST I know I just posted the table, but honestly making sense of the maelstrom that is the middle of that table is impossible after four games. The key figures are 16 points, which was enough to qualify for the top eight last season; and 9 points, which may just about get you into the top 24, and thus the playoff round.
 It was 11 points for the top 24 in 2024/25, mind you. Manchester United – beware.

 Share 2h ago 14.41 EST Full-time scores in earlier games
 AEK Athens 2-3 Real Madrid
 Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool
 Two really entertaining affairs in which the less-fancied host looked set to clinch a result against the odds – until Fede Valverde scored in stoppage time to seal three points for Real Madrid, preserving their perfect start to this Champions League group stage, and breaking Athenian hearts. Only the Spanish giants and PSG have won four from four now.
 Liverpool had three consecutive wins before tonight, but despite leading twice against Fenerbahce, they were pegged back and then stunned by Vedat Muriqi’s winner. It’s a famous night for former Liverpool favourite Dirk Kuyt, now in charge of Fenerbahce.
 If the later games can be anything like these two in terms of entertainment value we’re all in for a cracking couple of hours. Strangely, Real Betis have the chance to join Real Madrid and PSG on top of the pile, if they win in Dortmund.
 Share 2h ago 14.28 EST In more logical news, Kylian Mbappé has found the net for Real Madrid, so Mourinho’s men could still dig themselves out of an almighty Champions League hole.
 Not many would have put money on neither Liverpool nor Madrid winning their games this evening, mind. Less than 10 minutes remaining in both.
 Share 2h ago 14.25 EST 3-2 Fener. Goodness me. It’s bedlam in Istanbul. What’s happened to Liverpool in the past few minutes?
 Share 2h ago 14.21 EST Scratch that, Fenerbahce get themselves quickly level – as they did in the first half. This time Gakpo is at fault, and Archie Brown profits for the Turkish side. (2-2)
 And big big news in Athens … AEK have scored! Stavros Pilios smashes home after a quick counterattack. Good grief, could Real Madrid really lose to the lowly Greek outfit? (2-1)
 Share 2h ago 14.16 EST A potentially big goal for Liverpool: Alexander Isak jumps straight off the substitutes’ bench to nod Andoni Iraola’s men ahead in Istanbul. Good play from fellow sub Cody Gakpo to stand up a delicious cross that was waiting to be headed home. (1-2)
 No such luck for Real Madrid in Athens, although José Mourinho has brought on Endrick and Federico Valverde in search of a winner. (1-1)
 Share 2h ago 14.11 EST A couple of Arsenal-related reads for you , as we count down to kick-off in the Czech capital. Can the Gunners reach 10 points from their first four games of the Champions League ?
 A win tonight would do just that.
 (Saliba is on the bench tonight, by the way, after Arteta talked up a possible return.)
 Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson Read more Arteta backs Saliba’s readiness to return for Arsenal at Slavia Prague Read more Share 2h ago 14.02 EST Speaking of AEK Athens … the Greek champions are holding Real Madrid 1-1 after roughly an hour. Jude Bellingham scored a STUNNING flick for Los Blancos – do check that out on the ol’ socials. And Liverpool are still locked at the same scoreline with Fenerbahce. The big boys not having everything their own way as it stands in those early games.
 Share 2h ago 13.55 EST City have made five changes from the team Enzo Maresca picked at the weekend, which lost 1-0 at home to Brighton. Nico O’Reilly hasn’t been a regular this season so it will be interesting to see how he fares at left-back, especially from an England perspective with the youngster still favoured in that role by Thomas Tuchel, though under pressure from Newcastle’s Lewis Hall.
 Phil Foden, who comes in for Jérémy Doku, will be another player keen to impress the England boss. Three of Foden’s four goals in all competitions this season came in a single Champions League game against AEK Athens last month.
 View image in fullscreen Phil Foden spoke to the media before Manchester City’s game in Leipzig. Photograph: DPA/PA Share Updated at  13.58 EST 3h ago 13.52 EST Team news from selected games
 RB Leipzig v Manchester City 
 RB Leipzig: Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; Banzuzo, El Aynaoui, Baumgartner; Gruda, Nusa, Rômulo. 
 Man City: Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Guéhi, O’Reilly; Anderson, Fernández; Ndiaye, Cherki, Foden; Haaland. 
 Slavia Prague v Arsenal 
 Slavia: Domchak; Holes, Zima, Vicek; Nowak, Moses, Sadilek, Kublak; Ayaosi, Suleiman, Sturm. 
 Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapié; Zubimendi, Rice, Merino; Madueke, Eze, Gyökeres. 
 Other games 
 Elsewhere, the Como team lining up at Lens looking for their third victory in the Champions League includes the superstar attacker Nico Paz, with ex-Newcastle man Florian Thauvin the man to watch for Lens . Meanwhile in-form Dortmund include Jobe Bellingham and Fabio Silva in their lineup to take on Antony’s Real Betis at the Westfalenstadion.
 Share Updated at  13.57 EST 3h ago 13.38 EST It’s 1-1 at half-time in Istanbul after a deflected strike apiece for Fenerbahce and Liverpool.
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool: Champions League – live Read more Share 3h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 For all the valid arguments against the Champions League group phase using a ‘Swiss model’ – and there are many – it has at least produced an entertaining spectacle, with the bigger teams facing each other more regularly and the games, especially this season, producing lots of goals. Last night Manchester United discovered a new brand of chaos-ball to take centre stage, and take some heat off Michael Carrick, while Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain reminded us all why they are considered two of the favourites for the trophy, scoring nine goals between them.
 Tonight, it’s the turn of Manchester City and Arsenal , who are away at RB Leipzig and Slavia Prague respectively, with both expected to win and win well. Even away from the English teams, there are some interesting ties: Borussia Dortmund v Real Betis and Porto v Napoli stand out as having the potential to thrill, and there’s also Lens v Como, PSV v Club Brugge and the titans of Viking meeting the giants of Sabah .
 In the mean-time, Fenerbahce v Liverpool is ongoing – follow updates of that right here , as is AEK Athens v Real Madrid. We’ll follow those two games til their conclusion before getting stuck into the 8pm (GMT) games.
 So that’s tonight’s football. Watch it – well, some of it. Or follow along on tonight’s clockwatch to keep tabs on pretty much all of it. We’ll bring you some of the team news headlines next.
